metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: This is Solomon’s Song of Songs. The Bride
units.rightText: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
leftNotes: 1:1 Most translators add subheadings for speaker identifications such as The Bride, The Groom, and The Friends based on the gender and number of the Hebrew words.

units.leftText: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is more delightful than wine.
units.rightText: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; For thy love is better than wine.

units.leftText: The fragrance of your perfume is pleasing; your name is like perfume poured out. No wonder the maidens adore you.
units.rightText: Thine oils have a goodly fragrance; Thy name is as oil poured forth; Therefore do the virgins love thee.

units.leftText: Take me away with you— let us hurry! May the king bring me to his chambers. The Friends We will rejoice and delight in you; we will praise your love more than wine. The Bride It is only right that they adore you.
units.rightText: Draw me; we will run after thee: The king hath brought me into his chambers; We will be glad and rejoice in thee; We will make mention of thy love more than of wine: Rightly do they love thee.

units.leftText: I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
units.rightText: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, As the tents of Kedar, As the curtains of Solomon.

units.leftText: Do not stare because I am dark, for the sun has gazed upon me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; they made me a keeper of the vineyards, but my own vineyard I have neglected.
units.rightText: Look not upon me, because I am swarthy, Because the sun hath scorched me. My mother’s sons were incensed against me; They made me keeper of the vineyards; But mine own vineyard have I not kept.

units.leftText: Tell me, O one I love, where do you pasture your sheep? Where do you rest them at midday? Why should I be like a veiled woman beside the flocks of your companions? The Friends
units.rightText: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, Where thou feedest thy flock, Where thou makest it to rest at noon: For why should I be as one that is veiled Beside the flocks of thy companions?

units.leftText: If you do not know, O fairest of women, follow the tracks of the flock, and graze your young goats near the tents of the shepherds. The Bridegroom
units.rightText: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, Go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, And feed thy kids beside the shepherds’ tents.

units.leftText: I compare you, my darling, to a mare among Pharaoh’s chariots.
units.rightText: I have compared thee, O my love, To a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.

units.leftText: Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels. The Friends
units.rightText: Thy cheeks are comely with plaits of hair, Thy neck with strings of jewels.

units.leftText: We will make you ornaments of gold, studded with beads of silver. The Bride
units.rightText: We will make thee plaits of gold With studs of silver.

units.leftText: While the king was at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
units.rightText: While the king sat at his table, My spikenard sent forth its fragrance.

units.leftText: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.
units.rightText: My beloved is unto me as a bundle of myrrh, That lieth betwixt my breasts.

units.leftText: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi. The Bridegroom
units.rightText: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of henna-flowers In the vineyards of En-gedi.

units.leftText: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves. The Bride
units.rightText: Behold, thou art fair, my love; Behold thou art fair; Thine eyes are as doves.

units.leftText: How handsome you are, my beloved! Oh, how delightful! The soft grass is our bed. The Bridegroom
units.rightText: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: Also our couch is green.

units.leftText: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are fragrant firs.
units.rightText: The beams of our house are cedars, And our rafters are firs.

units.leftText: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valley. The Bridegroom
units.rightText: I am a rose of Sharon, A lily of the valleys.
leftNotes: 2:1 Sharon Plain is a region in the coastal plain of Israel

units.leftText: Like a lily among the thorns is my darling among the maidens. The Bride
units.rightText: As a lily among thorns, So is my love among the daughters.

units.leftText: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.
units.rightText: As the apple-tree among the trees of the wood, So is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, And his fruit was sweet to my taste.

units.leftText: He has brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me is love.
units.rightText: He brought me to the banqueting-house, And his banner over me was love.

units.leftText: Sustain me with raisins; refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.
units.rightText: Stay ye me with raisins, refresh me with apples; For I am sick from love.

units.leftText: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
units.rightText: His left hand is under my head, And his right hand doth embrace me.

units.leftText: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.
units.rightText: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake my love, Until he please.

units.leftText: Listen! My beloved approaches. Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.
units.rightText: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh, Leaping upon the mountains, Skipping upon the hills.

units.leftText: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.
units.rightText: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: Behold, he standeth behind our wall; He looketh in at the windows; He glanceth through the lattice.

units.leftText: My beloved calls to me, “Arise, my darling. Come away with me, my beautiful one.
units.rightText: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.

units.leftText: For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.
units.rightText: For, lo, the winter is past; The rain is over and gone;

units.leftText: The flowers have appeared in the countryside; the season of singing has come, and the cooing of turtledoves is heard in our land.
units.rightText: The flowers appear on the earth; The time of the singing of birds is come, And the voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land;

units.leftText: The fig tree ripens its figs; the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. Arise, come away, my darling; come away with me, my beautiful one.” The Bridegroom
units.rightText: The fig-tree ripeneth her green figs, And the vines are in blossom; They give forth their fragrance. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.

units.leftText: O my dove in the clefts of the rock, in the crevices of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is lovely. The Friends
units.rightText: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, In the covert of the steep place, Let me see thy countenance, Let me hear thy voice; For sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.

units.leftText: Catch for us the foxes— the little foxes that ruin the vineyards— for our vineyards are in bloom. The Bride
units.rightText: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, That spoil the vineyards; For our vineyards are in blossom.

units.leftText: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.
units.rightText: My beloved is mine, and I am his: He feedeth his flock among the lilies.

units.leftText: Before the day breaks and shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of Bether.
units.rightText: Until the day be cool, and the shadows flee away, Turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart Upon the mountains of Bether.

units.leftText: On my bed at night I sought the one I love; I sought him, but did not find him.
units.rightText: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

units.leftText: I will arise now and go about the city, through the streets and squares. I will seek the one I love. So I sought him but did not find him.
units.rightText: I said, I will rise now, and go about the city; In the streets and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

units.leftText: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city: “Have you seen the one I love?”
units.rightText: The watchmen that go about the city found me; To whom I said, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?

units.leftText: I had just passed them when I found the one I love. I held him and would not let go until I had brought him to my mother’s house, to the chamber of the one who conceived me.
units.rightText: It was but a little that I passed from them, When I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, Until I had brought him into my mother’s house, And into the chamber of her that conceived me.

units.leftText: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right. Solomon Arrives on His Wedding Day
units.rightText: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake my love, Until he please.

units.leftText: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense from all the spices of the merchant?
units.rightText: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness Like pillars of smoke, Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, With all powders of the merchant?

units.leftText: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage, escorted by sixty of the mightiest men of Israel.
units.rightText: Behold, it is the litter of Solomon; Threescore mighty men are about it, Of the mighty men of Israel.
leftNotes: 3:7 That is, the couch on which servants carry a king

units.leftText: All are skilled with the sword, experienced in warfare. Each has his sword at his side prepared for the terror of the night.
units.rightText: They all handle the sword, and are expert in war: Every man hath his sword upon his thigh, Because of fear in the night.

units.leftText: King Solomon has made his carriage out of the timber of Lebanon.
units.rightText: King Solomon made himself a palanquin Of the wood of Lebanon.

units.leftText: He has made its posts of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple fabric. Its interior is inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: He made the pillars thereof of silver, The bottom thereof of gold, the seat of it of purple, The midst thereof being paved with love, From the daughters of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Come out, O daughters of Zion, and gaze at King Solomon, wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding— the day of his heart’s rejoicing.
units.rightText: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon, With the crown wherewith his mother hath crowned him In the day of his espousals, And in the day of the gladness of his heart.

units.leftText: How beautiful you are, my darling— how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead.
units.rightText: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; Thine eyes are as doves behind thy veil. Thy hair is as a flock of goats, That lie along the side of mount Gilead.

units.leftText: Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.
units.rightText: Thy teeth are like a flock of ewes that are newly shorn, Which are come up from the washing, Whereof every one hath twins, And none is bereaved among them.

units.leftText: Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon, and your mouth is lovely. Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.
units.rightText: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, And thy mouth is comely. Thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate Behind thy veil.

units.leftText: Your neck is like the tower of David, built with rows of stones; on it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.
units.rightText: Thy neck is like the tower of David Builded for an armory, Whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, All the shields of the mighty men.

units.leftText: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle grazing among the lilies.
units.rightText: Thy two breasts are like two fawns That are twins of a roe, Which feed among the lilies.

units.leftText: Before the day breaks and the shadows flee, I will make my way to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
units.rightText: Until the day be cool, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, And to the hill of frankincense.

units.leftText: You are altogether beautiful, my darling; in you there is no flaw.
units.rightText: Thou art all fair, my love; And there is no spot in thee.

units.leftText: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon! Descend from the peak of Amana, from the summits of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.
units.rightText: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, With me from Lebanon: Look from the top of Amana, From the top of Senir and Hermon, From the lions’ dens, From the mountains of the leopards.

units.leftText: You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your neck.
units.rightText: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my bride; Thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, With one chain of thy neck.

units.leftText: How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is much better than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than all spices.
units.rightText: How fair is thy love, my sister, my bride! How much better is thy love than wine! And the fragrance of thine oils than all manner of spices!

units.leftText: Your lips, my bride, drip sweetness like the honeycomb; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the aroma of Lebanon.
units.rightText: Thy lips, O my bride, drop as the honeycomb: Honey and milk are under thy tongue; And the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

units.leftText: My sister, my bride, you are a garden locked up, a spring enclosed, a fountain sealed.
units.rightText: A garden shut up is my sister, my bride; A spring shut up, a fountain sealed.

units.leftText: Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates with the choicest of fruits, with henna and nard,
units.rightText: Thy shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits; Henna with spikenard plants,

units.leftText: with nard and saffron, with calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of frankincense tree, with myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.
units.rightText: Spikenard and saffron, Calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; Myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices.

units.leftText: You are a garden spring, a well of fresh water flowing down from Lebanon. The Bride
units.rightText: Thou art a fountain of gardens, A well of living waters, And flowing streams from Lebanon.
leftNotes: 4:15 Or flowing water or living water

units.leftText: Awake, O north wind, and come, O south wind. Breathe on my garden and spread the fragrance of its spices. Let my beloved come into his garden and taste its choicest fruits.
units.rightText: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; Blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, And eat his precious fruits.

units.leftText: I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. The Friends Eat, O friends, and drink; drink freely, O beloved. The Bride
units.rightText: I am come into my garden, my sister, my bride: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends; Drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.

units.leftText: I sleep, but my heart is awake. A sound! My beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night.”
units.rightText: I was asleep, but my heart waked: It is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; For my head is filled with dew, My locks with the drops of the night.

units.leftText: I have taken off my robe — must I put it back on? I have washed my feet— must I soil them again?
units.rightText: I have put off my garment; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?

units.leftText: My beloved put his hand to the latch; my heart pounded for him.
units.rightText: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, And my heart was moved for him.

units.leftText: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh on the handles of the bolt.
units.rightText: I rose up to open to my beloved; And my hands dropped with myrrh, And my fingers with liquid myrrh, Upon the handles of the bolt.

units.leftText: I opened for my beloved, but he had turned and gone. My heart sank at his departure. I sought him but did not find him. I called, but he did not answer.
units.rightText: I opened to my beloved; But my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone. My soul had failed me when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

units.leftText: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city. They beat me and bruised me; they took away my cloak, those guardians of the walls.
units.rightText: The watchmen that go about the city found me, They smote me, they wounded me; The keepers of the walls took away my mantle from me.

units.leftText: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you, if you find my beloved, tell him I am sick with love. The Friends
units.rightText: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, If ye find my beloved, That ye tell him, that I am sick from love.

units.leftText: How is your beloved better than others, O most beautiful among women? How is your beloved better than another, that you charge us so? The Bride
units.rightText: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? What is thy beloved more than another beloved, That thou dost so adjure us?

units.leftText: My beloved is dazzling and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.
units.rightText: My beloved is white and ruddy, The chiefest among ten thousand.

units.leftText: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy and black as a raven.
units.rightText: His head is as the most fine gold; His locks are bushy, and black as a raven.

units.leftText: His eyes are like doves beside the streams of water, bathed in milk and mounted like jewels.
units.rightText: His eyes are like doves beside the water-brooks, Washed with milk, and fitly set.

units.leftText: His cheeks are like beds of spice, towers of perfume. His lips are like lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh.
units.rightText: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, As banks of sweet herbs: His lips are as lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.

units.leftText: His arms are rods of gold set with beryl. His body is polished ivory bedecked with sapphires.
units.rightText: His hands are as rings of gold set with beryl: His body is as ivory work overlaid with sapphires.

units.leftText: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, as majestic as the cedars.
units.rightText: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: His aspect is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

units.leftText: His mouth is most sweet; he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: His mouth is most sweet; Yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Which way has he turned? We will seek him with you. The Bride
units.rightText: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? Whither hath thy beloved turned him, That we may seek him with thee?

units.leftText: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies.
units.rightText: My beloved is gone down to his garden, To the beds of spices, To feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

units.leftText: I belong to my beloved and he belongs to me; he pastures his flock among the lilies. The Bridegroom
units.rightText: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine: He feedeth his flock among the lilies.

units.leftText: You are as beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah, as lovely as Jerusalem, as majestic as troops with banners.
units.rightText: Thou art fair, O my love, as Tirzah, Comely as Jerusalem, Terrible as an army with banners.

units.leftText: Turn your eyes away from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Gilead.
units.rightText: Turn away thine eyes from me, For they have overcome me. Thy hair is as a flock of goats, That lie along the side of Gilead.

units.leftText: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.
units.rightText: Thy teeth are like a flock of ewes, Which are come up from the washing; Whereof every one hath twins, And none is bereaved among them.

units.leftText: Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.
units.rightText: Thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate Behind thy veil.

units.leftText: There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and maidens without number,
units.rightText: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, And virgins without number.

units.leftText: but my dove, my perfect one, is unique, the favorite of the mother who bore her. The maidens see her and call her blessed; the queens and concubines sing her praises. The Friends
units.rightText: My dove, my undefiled, is but one; She is the only one of her mother; She is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and called her blessed; Yea, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

units.leftText: Who is this who shines like the dawn, as fair as the moon, as bright as the sun, as majestic as the stars in procession? The Bridegroom
units.rightText: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, Fair as the moon, Clear as the sun, Terrible as an army with banners?

units.leftText: I went down to the walnut grove to see the blossoms of the valley, to see if the vines were budding or the pomegranates were in bloom.
units.rightText: I went down into the garden of nuts, To see the green plants of the valley, To see whether the vine budded, And the pomegranates were in flower.

units.leftText: Before I realized it, my desire had set me among the royal chariots of my people. The Friends
units.rightText: Before I was aware, my soul set me Among the chariots of my princely people.
leftNotes: 6:12 Or among the chariots of Amminadab

units.leftText: Come back, come back, O Shulammite! Come back, come back, that we may gaze upon you. The Bridegroom Why do you look at the Shulammite, as on the dance of Mahanaim ?
units.rightText: Return, return, O Shulammite; Return, return, that we may look upon thee. Why will ye look upon the Shulammite, As upon the dance of Mahanaim?
leftNotes: 6:13 Or the dance of the two camps

units.leftText: How beautiful are your sandaled feet, O daughter of the prince! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the handiwork of a master.
units.rightText: How beautiful are thy feet in sandals, O prince’s daughter! Thy rounded thighs are like jewels, The work of the hands of a skilful workman.

units.leftText: Your navel is a rounded goblet; it never lacks blended wine. Your waist is a mound of wheat encircled by the lilies.
units.rightText: Thy body is like a round goblet, Wherein no mingled wine is wanting: Thy waist is like a heap of wheat Set about with lilies.

units.leftText: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
units.rightText: Thy two breasts are like two fawns That are twins of a roe.

units.leftText: Your neck is like a tower made of ivory; your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim; your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, facing toward Damascus.
units.rightText: Thy neck is like the tower of ivory; Thine eyes as the pools in Heshbon, By the gate of Bath-rabbim; Thy nose is like the tower of Lebanon Which looketh toward Damascus.

units.leftText: Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel, the hair of your head like purple threads; the king is captured in your tresses.
units.rightText: Thy head upon thee is like Carmel, And the hair of thy head like purple; The king is held captive in the tresses thereof.

units.leftText: How fair and pleasant you are, O love, with your delights!
units.rightText: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!

units.leftText: Your stature is like a palm tree; your breasts are clusters of fruit.
units.rightText: This thy stature is like to a palm-tree, And thy breasts to its clusters.

units.leftText: I said, “I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit.” May your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the fragrance of your breath like apples,
units.rightText: I said, I will climb up into the palm-tree, I will take hold of the branches thereof: Let thy breasts be as clusters of the vine, And the smell of thy breath like apples,

units.leftText: and your mouth like the finest wine. The Bride May it flow smoothly to my beloved, gliding gently over lips and teeth.
units.rightText: And thy mouth like the best wine, That goeth down smoothly for my beloved, Gliding through the lips of those that are asleep.
leftNotes: 7:9 LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate; Hebrew gliding gently over lips as we sleep

units.leftText: I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me.
units.rightText: I am my beloved’s; And his desire is toward me.

units.leftText: Come, my beloved, let us go to the countryside; let us spend the night among the wildflowers.
units.rightText: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; Let us lodge in the villages.
leftNotes: 7:11 Or among the henna blossoms or in the villages

units.leftText: Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vine has budded, if the blossom has opened, if the pomegranates are in bloom — there I will give you my love.
units.rightText: Let us get up early to the vineyards; Let us see whether the vine hath budded, And its blossom is open, And the pomegranates are in flower: There will I give thee my love.

units.leftText: The mandrakes send forth a fragrance, and at our door is every delicacy, new as well as old, that I have treasured up for you, my beloved.
units.rightText: The mandrakes give forth fragrance; And at our doors are all manner of precious fruits, new and old, Which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.

units.leftText: O that you were to me like a brother who nursed at my mother’s breasts! If I found you outdoors, I would kiss you, and no one would despise me.
units.rightText: Oh that thou wert as my brother, That sucked the breasts of my mother! When I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; Yea, and none would despise me.

units.leftText: I would lead you and bring you to the house of my mother who taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the nectar of my pomegranates.
units.rightText: I would lead thee, and bring thee into my mother’s house, Who would instruct me; I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine, Of the juice of my pomegranate.

units.leftText: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
units.rightText: His left hand should be under my head, And his right hand should embrace me.

units.leftText: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right. The Friends
units.rightText: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, That ye stir not up, nor awake my love, Until he please.

units.leftText: Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? The Bride I roused you under the apple tree; there your mother conceived you; there she travailed and brought you forth.
units.rightText: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, Leaning upon her beloved? Under the apple-tree I awakened thee: There thy mother was in travail with thee, There was she in travail that brought thee forth.

units.leftText: Set me as a seal over your heart, as a seal upon your arm. For love is as strong as death, its jealousy as unrelenting as Sheol. Its sparks are fiery flames, the fiercest blaze of all.
units.rightText: Set me as a seal upon thy heart, As a seal upon thine arm: For love is strong as death; Jealousy is cruel as Sheol; The flashes thereof are flashes of fire, A very flame of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Mighty waters cannot quench love; rivers cannot sweep it away. If a man were to give all the wealth of his house for love, his offer would be utterly scorned. The Friends
units.rightText: Many waters cannot quench love, Neither can floods drown it: If a man would give all the substance of his house for love, He would utterly be contemned.

units.leftText: We have a little sister, and her breasts are not yet grown. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?
units.rightText: We have a little sister, And she hath no breasts: What shall we do for our sister In the day when she shall be spoken for?

units.leftText: If she is a wall, we will build a tower of silver upon her. If she is a door, we will enclose her with panels of cedar. The Bride
units.rightText: If she be a wall, We will build upon her a turret of silver: And if she be a door, We will inclose her with boards of cedar.

units.leftText: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. So I have become in his eyes like one who brings peace.
units.rightText: I am a wall, and my breasts like the towers thereof: Then was I in his eyes as one that found peace.

units.leftText: Solomon had a vineyard in Baal-hamon. He leased it to the tenants. For its fruit, each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver.
units.rightText: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; He let out the vineyard unto keepers; Every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand pieces of silver.
leftNotes: 8:11 Hebrew a thousand of silver; that is, approximately 25.1 pounds or 11.4 kilograms of silver

units.leftText: But my own vineyard is mine to give; the thousand shekels are for you, O Solomon, and two hundred are for those who tend its fruit. The Bridegroom
units.rightText: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: Thou, O Solomon, shalt have the thousand, And those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.

units.leftText: You who dwell in the gardens, my companions are listening for your voice. Let me hear it! The Bride
units.rightText: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, The companions hearken for thy voice: Cause me to hear it.

units.leftText: Come away, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices.
units.rightText: Make haste, my beloved, And be thou like to a roe or to a young hart Upon the mountains of spices.
